title: A Narrow Garden
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：taste　|　正文 359 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 taste 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: My grandmother's garden grew only three things: cabbage, a narrow strip of wheat, and the apple tree her mother had planted. Everything that came out of it had a stronger ① taste than anything bought in a shop. I liked that as a child, and I understand it better now.

She never used fertiliser and never watered the plants after June. 'A dry root is a sweeter root,' she would say, handing me a leaf and making me have a ② taste of it before we picked anything. We ③ tasted half the garden most afternoons and spat most of it into the grass. Nothing in that garden was wasted; even the outer leaves went into the pot, and nothing she grew ever tasted quite the same twice.

The apples arrived late and small, split by the rain, and every one of them ④ tasted of something sharper than sugar. My mother made jam from the windfalls; my grandmother refused to touch it, saying that jam hides the fruit. What she wanted, I think, was for us to notice rather than to enjoy.

In her last summer she lost most of her ⑤ taste — the doctor said it was the medicine — and she stopped cooking almost entirely. Our neighbour brought soup twice a week. She ate it, thanked her, and said very little, which was not like her. A person who has cooked for sixty years does not stop quietly.

At her funeral more people spoke about that garden than about anything else. One old man said she had taught him what a tomato is supposed to ⑥ taste like, and three others nodded at once. She was never trying to impress anybody; what she had was not skill alone but ⑦ taste. Those hard little apples were never ⑧ to my taste when I was nine, though I have looked for that sharp ⑨ taste in shops every autumn since and have never found it. These days I try to ⑩ taste everything twice before deciding whether I like it — taste her apples once and you will never forget them — which is more or less what she taught me to do with a leaf.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: D. n. （少量的）品尝；试味（have a taste of）
F. 固定搭配：taste of 有……的味道
G. 固定搭配：to one's taste 合某人的口味
H. 固定搭配：taste like 尝起来像……

items.q: had a stronger taste than anything bought in a shop
making me have a taste of it
tasted of something sharper than sugar
she lost most of her taste
what a tomato is supposed to taste like
what she had was not skill alone but taste
were never to my taste when I was nine
I try to taste everything twice

answers.why: a stronger taste 被比较级修饰、后接 than 比较对象，是名词“味道、滋味”。
have a taste of sth 意为“尝一口”，是名词性的“少量品尝”，祖母先让作者在决定是否采摘前试味。
taste＋宾语 half the garden，是动词“尝”，描写祖孙俩每天下午尝半个菜园。
taste of＋味道，意为“有……的味道”，此处说苹果有一股比糖更烈的味道。
lose one's taste 指失去“味觉”，与药的副作用相关，不是失去品味。
taste like＋从句，意为“尝起来像……”，老人说祖母教会他西红柿本该是什么味。
not skill but taste 与 skill 并列，指“品味、鉴赏力”，强调她的判断力而非手艺。
to one's taste 意为“合某人口味”，作者九岁时并不喜欢那些硬苹果。
that sharp taste 指那种强烈的滋味，与第 1 题同为名词“味道”。
taste everything twice 是动词“尝”，作者如今做事前会多试一次。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 自家种的卷心菜味道比店里买的更浓。（taste n.）
决定之前，祖母让我先尝一口。（have a taste of）
我们几乎每天下午都尝半个菜园。（taste v.）
那些苹果有一股比糖更烈的味道。（taste of）
服药之后，她几乎失去了味觉。（lose one's taste）
外婆教我知道了西红柿应该是什么味道。（taste like）
answers: Home-grown cabbage has a stronger taste than anything bought in a shop.
Before deciding, my grandmother made me have a taste of it.
We tasted half the garden almost every afternoon.
Those apples tasted of something sharper than sugar.
After taking the medicine she lost almost all of her taste.
My grandmother taught me what a tomato is supposed to taste like.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 taste 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: My grandmother grew cabbage, a strip of wheat and one apple tree, and everything had a stronger taste than shop food.
She made me have a taste of every leaf before we picked anything, saying a dry root is a sweeter root.
We tasted half the garden each afternoon, and her apples always tasted of something sharper than sugar.
In her last summer she lost most of her taste and stopped cooking, which was not like her at all.
She never cooked jam, because jam hides the fruit, and an old neighbour once said she taught him what a tomato should taste like.
Those hard little apples were never to my taste at nine, but I still taste everything twice before deciding, and then look for that sharp taste every autumn.
